target_customer: Air passengers with delayed, cancelled or overbooked flights who are owed compensation
problem: Airlines made compensation claims slow and confusing, so most eligible passengers never claimed. AirHelp files and fights claims for a success fee.
business_model: Success fee on recovered compensation (original application 25 percent; later sources say 35 percent)
product_category: Consumer legal tech, flight compensation claims

founders.name: Henrik Zillmer
previous_startups: More than ten startups in insurance, travel, software and e-commerce per YC page
founders.background_notes: YC page: launched Zalora in eight countries and grew it from 5 to 2,000 employees in under a year. Wikipedia lists a 2013 co-founding; other co-founders not confirmed in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Flight disruption database, claim intake and case management; the hard part was legal and operational process, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Claim volume, legal partnerships and passenger data build up over time, but rivals ran the same EU261 model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition of AirHelp; it later co-founded a passenger rights trade group with rival portals and acquired Dutch rail claims firm Trein Vertraging in late 2025.

market_need_then: EU Regulation 261 gave passengers up to 600 euros per disrupted flight but few claimed; the YC application described a database of disrupted flights and notifications of passenger rights.

branding.domain_note: Uses airhelp.com with country domains such as airhelp.de.

identity.voice_and_tone: Helpful ally for travelers; ads stress no win no fee and up to 600 euros

branding.brand_signature: No win, no fee compensation up to 600 euros
branding.community_and_virality: Ran brand tracking against competitors with Latana and heavy advertising; no mascot or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Plain descriptive name with wide consumer awareness from advertising and brand tracking; evidence does not show the name itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: AirHelp joined YC in Winter 2014, raised a $12M Series A in August 2016 and a $9M Series B-2 in 2021, and took a minority investment from Abry Partners in March 2025. It claimed to have helped 900,000 passengers by 2016 and is an active, scaled company, with the main risks being regulatory change, airline disputes and rival claim portals.
notes: Competitors list left empty: searches found only undated or later pages (Flightright, EUclaim, ClaimFlights from 2015, others later), none dated near the 2014 batch. Seed in 2014 shown by aggregators as $220K (March) or $400K (May), not verified so not recorded. Investor names for Series A beyond Khosla and Williams come from a citybizlist report seen in a search snippet. Series B-2 comes from Wikipedia only (flagged promotional); aggregators call the 2025 Abry deal a secondary transaction and one listing says $350M for 20 percent, unverified. Co-founder Nicolas Michaelsen appears in a search snippet only and is not listed. TechCrunch 2016 calls Zillmer co-founder and CEO while Wikipedia lists Tomasz Pawliszyn as CEO. Outcome search found no layoffs or fines; a November 2025 supply chain security incident was reported by the company.
